correctness.rationale: Explicit cylindrical velocity and acceleration, nonzero speed, and cross-product yield the exact integral. Fuller’s known zero set localizes a unique zero. Independent partial derivatives of the cross product at this point are orthogonal with lengths D*V and p*r* q²(1+r*). The local square-root integral produces C=(D*V)²/[p*r* q²(1+r*) V²]=D^4/[p³ q²(2p²+q²)], and analyticity off the zero yields the stated C1/not-C2 expansion. Uniform v and a estimates bound the high-q integrand error by O(q^-1), even at the zero; elliptic identity and convexity give the stated profile and inverse. The extracted checker replay passed 183 main diagnostics plus 25 normal-form diagnostics. Finite checks are not a proof.

originality.rationale: Known inflection threshold and count are expressly credited to Fuller 1998. The distinct new content consists of two integrated total-curvature asymptotic theorems: a sharp fixed-winding logarithmic cusp coefficient and a uniform joint small-radius/high-winding elliptic crossover. Full-text comparisons to Fuller, Oberti–Ricca and Gerlach–Reiter–von der Mosel found no implication covering these asymptotics. Priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The known q simultaneous inflections create a natural unresolved singular regularity question for an important global geometric functional. The explicit coefficient quantifies curvature sensitivity near the inflection-bearing torus. The double scaling resolves the otherwise noncommuting small-radius and high-frequency limits, and an explicit strictly increasing elliptic profile reconstructs the scaled tube radius. These are nonroutine structural laws, not a numeric table or simple restatement of the known vanishing-curvature theorem.
